messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: detected spike in 5xx for /v1/generate in eu-west-2 (az2). Paging rotation started. priority=P1, impact=customer-visible errors and increased latency. paging: Priya -> Sam -> Kai.
Priya (oncall): saw the pager. I'm on it, joining now. saw spike ~10:12 UTC, error rate ~18% for the generation path.
Sam: I can grab traces. linking recent dashboards: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/requests?region=eu-west-2&route=/v1/generate
Kai: I already started a tcpdump on one of the az2 frontends. lots of reset (RST) seen to 10.0.45.0/24 (worker subnets) when crossing to nat-az1.
Priya (oncall): odd — we route az2 outbound via NAT-az2. could be route table drift. Dan (netinfra) you around?
Dan (netinfra): oncall — ping. running quick checks on route tables and NAT attachments.
SRE-Bot: deploy bot: terraform apply completed in eu-west-2 at 10:09:23 UTC by infra-automation (change id: tf-2026-4302).
Kai: stack-trace from frontend logs: "connect error: connection reset by peer" to 172.31.12.8:443 (nat instance IP) repeatedly.
Priya (oncall): looking at VPC console: route table rt-0a12 shows 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-az1 for subnets in az2 (should be nat-az2).
Dan (netinfra): confirming — terraform change replaced a route attachment after an AZ shuffle. NAT gateway detachment in az2 happened during apply. We're seeing route table association flipped to the wrong table.
Sam: impact: requests that require external APIs (model storage fetch, telemetry) from az2 frontends are intermittently failing. scale=~20% of generation requests hit az2 at peak.
Priya (oncall): mitigation plan A: rollback tf change to restore rt associations -> reattach nat-az2. plan B if rollback takes time: add emergency route pointing 0.0.0.0/0 -> nat-az2 elastic ip via route update (manual). which is faster?
Dan (netinfra): rollback via terraform is blocked by ongoing apply locks (automation just finished but state drift exists). manual route update is fastest. prepping commands.
Eli: prepping customer comm draft. will need ETA and workaround in channel.
Priya (oncall): do manual route update then verify conntrack on nat-az2. Kai — keep tcpdump running.
Dan (netinfra): performing manual route replace:
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0a12 --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id nat-0a2b3c4d
```
Dan (netinfra): applied. waiting for propagation (aws shows route propagated).
Kai: tcpdump shows RSTs falling to almost zero now. frontends start to see successful TLS handshakes.
Priya (oncall): monitoring error rate — dropping from 18% -> 3% over last 2 mins.
SRE-Bot: incident-bot: status update: mitigation applied (manual route replace). Continue monitoring 15m.
Sam: checking egress connection table on nat-az2, seeing a lot of TIME_WAIT but no conntrack exhaustion. CPU on nat-az2 spiked briefly during failover.
Priya (oncall): quick postmortem note: root cause appears to be an automated terraform rollout that inadvertently reassociated route tables during an AZ reconfiguration window. change made at 10:09:23. It attached the wrong route table to az2 subnets leaving them pointing at nat-az1.
Dan (netinfra): adding that NAT-az1 did not have enough cross-az path capacity for conntracking, causing resets when traffic crossed zones — explains the RSTs.
Eli: customer-facing note draft: "We experienced a partial outage for generation endpoints in eu-west-2 from ~10:12-10:28 UTC due to a configuration change affecting NAT routing in AZ2. Most requests recovered after a manual route fix. We are rolling back the automation and will provide a detailed postmortem." Thoughts?
Customer Success: Please include affected customers list and any customers we proactively contacted.
Priya (oncall): customer impact: 12 orgs saw increased 5xx, internal monitoring shows 98% of traffic recovered. will ask infra to run log query for top org ids.
Sam: running query now: top affected orgs: org-1012, org-2233, org-3301. exporting logs and sending to CS.
Dan (netinfra): starting full verification across AZs: checking other route tables for accidental re-assoc. found one more subnet in az3 with same drift (rtb-0b34). will fix it now.
Priya (oncall): open task: (1) revert the terraform change or update automation so re-assoc doesn't pick wrong table (2) add pre-apply validation to detect route table mismatches (3) add an automatic fallback policy to prefer local NAT for AZ egress and alert on cross-AZ egress spike.
SRE-Bot: note: created incident ticket INC-2026-042; assigned to NetInfra for rollback and to Runtime for verification.
Kai: continuing packet captures. no more RST bursts. latency back to normal for AZ2 callers.
Priya (oncall): handing off to Sam for monitoring and postmortem. Sam you're on for next 2 hours. I'm switching to follow mode.
Sam: ack taking handoff. I'll keep watch and coordinate the postmortem write-up.
Dan (netinfra): completed fixes on the other misassociated subnet. also scheduled an emergency tf plan review with automation team at 14:00 UTC.
Eli: CS notified customers and created followup tickets.
Customer Success: thanks — please add exact timestamps and affected org ids to the public comms.
Sam: final status: mitigation in place, residual error rate <0.5%, services stable for eu-west-2. will follow up with a full postmortem and remediation timeline.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: eu-west-2 NAT routing misassoc — mitigation applied and services recovered.
Priya (oncall): filing immediate blameless postmortem. tagging involved folks: @Dan, @Eli, @Sam.
Sam: adding timeline and initial RCA notes to the incident ticket.
Dan (netinfra): quick reminder: automation change that shuffled AZ mapping needs a canary and a pre-check for route table associations.
Priya (oncall): thanks everyone. closing thread once postmortem uploaded.
SRE-Bot: thread archived to incidents log at 11:07 UTC.
